## Technical Guide Details

### What Is a CAS Number and Why It Matters in Chemical Procurement
A CAS number is the unique Chemical Abstracts Service identifier used to specify chemical products. Learn how buyers use CAS numbers to verify and purchase intermediates.
A CAS Registry Number is a unique numeric identifier assigned to chemical substances by Chemical Abstracts Service. For procurement teams, it is the fastest way to remove ambiguity between product names, synonyms and commercial grades.
#### How a CAS Registry Number works
CAS numbers use a three-part hyphenated format, such as 4964-71-0. The number does not encode molecular structure; it points to a specific substance record in the CAS registry.
- CAS numbers remove ambiguity between names and synonyms
- The same compound can have many trade names but only one CAS number
- CAS search is the fastest way to verify the exact product you want to buy
#### Why CAS verification matters in procurement
Buyers use CAS numbers to compare quotations, review certificates of analysis and confirm regulatory documents. A mismatch between the product name and the CAS number can lead to the wrong intermediate reaching the pilot plant or production line.
#### Searching by CAS on malongchemicals.com
Enter the CAS number in the search bar and the site will take you directly to the matching product page. There you can check formula, molecular weight, purity and application notes before sending an inquiry.
#### Frequently asked questions
- Q: Is a CAS number the same as a product code?
  A: No. A CAS number identifies the chemical substance, while a supplier product code is an internal catalogue reference. The CAS number is the more reliable identifier for specification matching.
- Q: Can two different products share the same CAS number?
  A: No. Each CAS Registry Number is unique to one substance record. If two quotations show the same CAS number, the intended compound should be identical.
- Q: Do I need a CAS number to request a quote?
  A: It is recommended. Sharing the CAS number with quantity, purity and packaging requirements helps the supplier respond with a more accurate quotation.
- Guide URL: https://www.malongchemicals.com/guides/what-is-a-cas-number/

### How to Buy Chemical Intermediates from China: A Practical Guide
A step-by-step guide for international buyers sourcing CAS-listed chemical intermediates from China, including specifications, quotations, samples, packaging and shipping.
Buying chemical intermediates from China becomes much smoother when the specification is clear and the CAS number is verified. This guide covers the information buyers should prepare before contacting a supplier.
#### Define your specification first
Before contacting suppliers, write down the CAS number, target purity, quantity, packaging preference and destination country. A precise specification helps avoid quotation drift and shortens the confirmation cycle.
#### What to include in an inquiry
- CAS number and product name
- Quantity in grams or kilograms
- Target purity and required documents such as COA or HPLC data
- Packaging type and estimated shipping terms
- Timeline and destination country
#### From quotation to order
After receiving the quotation, confirm sample policy, MOQ, payment terms, packaging and delivery lead time. Keep the CAS number and specification in the order confirmation so both sides are aligned.
#### Frequently asked questions
- Q: Do you supply small research quantities?
  A: Contact us with the CAS number and target quantity. Our sales team can confirm current availability, packaging and MOQ for the specific product.
- Q: Can you provide a certificate of analysis?
  A: Please request COA and purity data together with your quotation inquiry so the supplier can confirm the documentation available for the batch.
- Q: What information speeds up a quotation?
  A: The most useful inquiry includes CAS number, quantity, purity target, packaging preference and destination country.
- Guide URL: https://www.malongchemicals.com/guides/how-to-buy-chemical-intermediates-from-china/

### Quinoline Intermediates for Pharmaceutical Synthesis
Quinoline and isoquinoline intermediates are used in antimalarial, antimicrobial and kinase inhibitor chemistry. See representative CAS products and how to select them.
Quinoline and isoquinoline scaffolds appear across pharmaceutical and agrochemical development. Halogenated, amino and methoxy derivatives provide the functional handles needed for further synthesis.
#### Why quinoline intermediates matter
The quinoline family supports antimalarial APIs such as Primaquine and Tafenoquine, fluoroquinolone antibiotics such as Ciprofloxacin and Levofloxacin, and quinoline-based antimicrobial and kinase inhibitor research.
#### Representative quinoline building blocks
- 5-Bromoquinoline (CAS 4964-71-0): brominated quinoline intermediate for antimalarial and antimicrobial quinoline API families
- 8-Iodoquinoline (CAS 1006-47-9): iodinated quinoline building block for functionalization and medicinal chemistry
- 6-Methoxy-8-aminoquinoline (CAS 90-52-8): methoxy-aminoquinoline intermediate used in antimalarial chemistry such as the Primaquine family
#### How to select a quinoline building block
Check the substitution position, halogen type and downstream target. Halogenated quinolines are usually selected for cross-coupling, while amino or methoxy derivatives are chosen when the functionality is already present in the target API.
#### Frequently asked questions
- Q: What are quinoline intermediates used for?
  A: They are used as building blocks for antimalarial, antimicrobial and kinase inhibitor APIs, as well as agrochemical and specialty chemical synthesis.
- Q: How do I choose between bromo and iodo quinoline intermediates?
  A: Iodo derivatives are generally more reactive in cross-coupling, while bromo derivatives offer a good balance of reactivity and stability. The choice depends on your synthesis route.
- Q: Can I request a specification for a quinoline intermediate?
  A: Yes. Send the CAS number and target quantity to our sales team to confirm purity, packaging and current availability.
- Guide URL: https://www.malongchemicals.com/guides/quinoline-intermediates-pharmaceutical-synthesis/

### 5-Bromoquinoline (CAS 4964-71-0): Applications and Supplier Guide
5-Bromoquinoline is a brominated quinoline intermediate used in pharmaceutical synthesis. Compare specifications, purity and sourcing notes for CAS 4964-71-0.
5-Bromoquinoline is one of our promoted quinoline building blocks. This guide summarizes the product specification, typical application areas and the information to confirm before ordering.
#### What is 5-bromoquinoline?
5-Bromoquinoline (CAS 4964-71-0) is a brominated quinoline building block. Its molecular formula is C9H6BrN and its molecular weight is 208.05.
#### Typical application areas
The product is used as a halogenated quinoline intermediate for antimalarial and antimicrobial quinoline API families, including Primaquine and Chloroquine chemistry, and for further functionalization in medicinal chemistry research.
#### Specification checklist
- CAS 4964-71-0
- Formula C9H6BrN
- Molecular weight 208.05
- Purity 98% min, with current batch COA to be confirmed by the supplier
#### Frequently asked questions
- Q: Is 5-bromoquinoline available for small research quantities?
  A: Please confirm your target quantity with our sales team; availability and packaging can be confirmed for the CAS number.
- Q: What is the difference between 5-bromoquinoline and 8-bromoquinoline?
  A: The bromine is attached at a different position of the quinoline ring, which changes the substitution pattern and downstream chemistry. The CAS number must be checked to avoid confusion.
- Q: Can I request COA and purity data?
  A: Yes. Include that request with your inquiry so the current batch documentation can be shared.

### Pyridine vs Pyrimidine Intermediates: How to Choose the Right Building Block
Compare pyridine and pyrimidine intermediates for pharmaceutical and agrochemical synthesis, including typical applications, substitution patterns and procurement considerations.
Pyridine and pyrimidine intermediates are both six-membered nitrogen heterocycles, but their different nitrogen content changes electronic properties and substitution patterns. This guide helps buyers compare the two families.
#### Structure and substitution
Pyridine has one nitrogen atom in the ring, while pyrimidine has two nitrogen atoms at the 1 and 3 positions. The difference changes electronic properties and the positions available for substitution.
#### Typical applications
- Pyridine and picoline derivatives are used in Vitamin B6 APIs such as Pyridoxine and in neonicotinoid agrochemical chemistry
- Pyrimidine intermediates are used in kinase inhibitor APIs and sulfonylurea herbicide synthesis
- Both families support pharmaceutical and agrochemical development across multiple CAS-listed building blocks
#### How to choose
Start from the downstream target, then verify the required substitution pattern, halogen or amino position and CAS number. When in doubt, share the target structure or API name with the supplier.
#### Frequently asked questions
- Q: Is pyridine or pyrimidine more reactive?
  A: Reactivity depends on the substitution pattern and reaction conditions rather than the heterocycle alone. The correct choice is usually driven by the downstream target.
- Q: Can the same synthesis use both pyridine and pyrimidine intermediates?
  A: They are different scaffolds, so the choice depends on the target molecule. Pyridine and pyrimidine building blocks are not interchangeable by CAS number.
- Q: How do I verify the CAS number?
  A: Use the CAS search bar on the website and compare the synonym list on the product page with your specification.
- Guide URL: https://www.malongchemicals.com/guides/pyridine-vs-pyrimidine-intermediates/

### Benzimidazole Intermediates for Pharmaceutical APIs
Benzimidazole intermediates support proton pump inhibitors, anticoagulants and anthelmintics. See representative CAS products and procurement guidance.
Benzimidazole is an important pharmaceutical scaffold. Brominated and methylated benzimidazole intermediates provide the handles needed for API synthesis and medicinal chemistry programs.
#### Why benzimidazole intermediates matter
Key targets include proton pump inhibitors Omeprazole and Esomeprazole, the anticoagulant Dabigatran etexilate, and anthelmintics such as Albendazole and Mebendazole.
#### Representative building blocks
- 5-Bromo-1H-benzimidazole (CAS 4887-88-1): brominated benzimidazole scaffold for API synthesis
- 5-Bromo-2-methyl-1H-benzoimidazole (CAS 1964-77-8): methylated bromobenzimidazole for further substitution
- Benzimidazole intermediates support proton pump inhibitor, anticoagulant and anthelmintic chemistry
#### Procurement notes
Confirm the exact substitution position and CAS number because benzimidazole isomers can be close in name but different in structure. Request COA and purity data for the batch before ordering.
#### Frequently asked questions
- Q: What APIs use benzimidazole intermediates?
  A: Examples include proton pump inhibitors, the anticoagulant Dabigatran etexilate and anthelmintic medicines.
- Q: Are brominated benzimidazoles suitable for cross-coupling?
  A: Brominated benzimidazoles are commonly used as coupling partners, but the reaction should be validated for the specific scaffold and substitution pattern.
- Q: Can you confirm current purity and packaging?
  A: Yes. Send the CAS number and target quantity to request current batch information.
- Guide URL: https://www.malongchemicals.com/guides/benzimidazole-intermediates-pharmaceuticals/

### Halogenated Aromatic Building Blocks for Cross-Coupling Chemistry
Brominated, chlorinated and iodinated aromatic intermediates enable Suzuki, Buchwald and related cross-coupling routes. Learn how to compare aryl halide building blocks.
Aryl halides are foundational building blocks in modern organic synthesis. The position and type of halogen determine how the building block can be used in cross-coupling and functional group chemistry.
#### Why aryl halides are useful
Brominated, chlorinated and iodinated aromatics are standard entry points for Suzuki, Buchwald and related cross-coupling reactions. Reactivity generally follows iodide greater than bromide greater than chloride, while bromides offer a good balance of stability and reactivity.
#### Representative products
- 1-Bromo-2,4-dimethoxybenzene (CAS 17715-69-4): dimethoxyaryl bromide for pharmaceutical and OLED/OPV monomer chemistry
- 2-Bromo-1,4-dimethoxybenzene (CAS 25245-34-5): regioisomeric dimethoxyaryl bromide
- 1,2-Dibromo-4-iodobenzene (CAS 909072-74-8): multihalogenated aryl building block for sequential cross-coupling
#### How to compare building blocks
Match the halogen positions to your planned disconnection, check purity and packaging, and verify the CAS number before ordering. For sequential coupling, different halogens allow stepwise functionalization.
#### Frequently asked questions
- Q: Which halogen should I choose for cross-coupling?
  A: The choice depends on reactivity, cost and selectivity. Bromides are common for aryl coupling, while iodides are more reactive and chlorides are more economical.
- Q: Are methoxy-substituted aryl bromides in the catalog?
  A: Yes. Examples include 1-bromo-2,4-dimethoxybenzene and 2-bromo-1,4-dimethoxybenzene, which differ by substitution position.
- Q: Can I request a multihalogenated building block?
  A: Confirm the CAS number and target quantity, and our team can check availability and specifications.
- Guide URL: https://www.malongchemicals.com/guides/halogenated-aromatic-building-blocks/

### Agrochemical Intermediates: Product Families and Procurement Guide
Agrochemical intermediates include halogenated anilines, pyridines, pyrimidines and nitriles used in fungicide, insecticide and herbicide synthesis.
Agrochemical synthesis uses a broad range of aromatic and heterocyclic intermediates. Understanding which product families map to fungicide, insecticide and herbicide chemistry helps buyers send more accurate inquiries.
#### Product families
Pyridine, pyrimidine, aniline and nitrile intermediates are common in agrochemical synthesis. The right building block depends on the target molecule and the functional groups required.
#### Representative applications
- Pyridine intermediates are used in neonicotinoid insecticide chemistry
- Halogenated anilines support fungicide families such as Bixafen and Boscalid
- Pyrimidine intermediates are used in sulfonylurea herbicide and antimicrobial chemistry
#### Sourcing guidance
Share the CAS number, target quantity and registration or specification requirements. Suppliers should be able to confirm purity, packaging and documentation before shipment.
#### Frequently asked questions
- Q: What intermediates are most common in agrochemical synthesis?
  A: Halogenated anilines, pyridines, pyrimidines and nitriles are all common, depending on the target class.
- Q: Do you supply intermediates for agrochemical registration batches?
  A: Please share the CAS number, quantity and documentation requirements so the supplier can confirm what is available.
- Q: Can one intermediate serve both pharma and agro applications?
  A: Yes. Some building blocks are used in both industries, so the application context matters less than the chemical specification.

What to check before ordering chemical intermediates: purity, COA, packaging, MOQ, shelf life and shipping. Practical questions for supplier qualification.

Ask about shelf life, storage conditions and transport restrictions. These details are especially important for international orders.

### Indazole and Indole Intermediates for Medicinal Chemistry
Indazole and indole scaffolds appear in oncology and CNS APIs. See representative building blocks and how to request current specifications.
Indazole and indole derivatives are widely used in medicinal chemistry programs. Their nitrogen-containing rings and substitution patterns make them valuable scaffolds for API development.
#### Why these scaffolds matter
These scaffolds are used in oncology APIs such as Axitinib, Pazopanib and Niraparib, and serotonin/triptan APIs such as Sumatriptan and Rizatriptan.
#### Representative building blocks
- 4-Methyl-1H-indazol-5-amine (CAS 101257-89-0): aminomethylindazole building block
- 5-Aminoindazole (CAS 19335-11-6): aminoindazole scaffold for medicinal chemistry
- 5-Iodo-1H-indazole (CAS 55919-82-9): iodinated indazole for cross-coupling
#### Sourcing notes
Confirm the exact substitution position and CAS number before ordering. Indazole and indole isomers can have very different reactivity and downstream targets.
#### Frequently asked questions
- Q: Are indazole and indole the same scaffold?
  A: No. They are different heterocycles. Indazole has two adjacent nitrogen atoms, while indole has one nitrogen atom in the five-membered ring.
- Q: What applications use these intermediates?
  A: Oncology APIs and CNS/neurology chemistry are common application areas.
- Q: Can I request a custom substitution?
  A: Share the target structure or CAS number and quantity; feasibility can be confirmed by our sales and technical team.
- Guide URL: https://www.malongchemicals.com/guides/indazole-indole-intermediates-medicinal-chemistry/

### CAS Number Search: How to Find and Verify Chemical Products
Use a CAS number search to locate a product quickly and confirm the compound identity. Guide covers exact-match searching, synonyms and supplier verification.
A CAS number is the most precise way to search for a chemical product. This guide explains how to use exact CAS search and what to check after finding the product page.
#### Use exact CAS search
Enter the hyphenated CAS number, such as 1006-47-9, in the search bar on malongchemicals.com. The site returns the exact matching product page.
#### Verify with synonyms
Check the synonym list on the product page because commercial names vary between markets. The CAS number is the stable identifier across regions.
#### What to do if the CAS is not found
Contact the sales team with the CAS number and target quantity. The product may be available on request or through custom synthesis.
#### Frequently asked questions
- Q: Should I include hyphens when searching a CAS number?
  A: Yes. Use the standard hyphenated format such as 4964-71-0 for the most reliable result.
- Q: Can I search by product name instead of CAS?
  A: The site supports browsing by product name and category, but exact CAS search is the fastest way to reach the intended product.
- Q: What if my CAS number returns no result?
  A: Send the CAS number to our sales team. The compound may be available on request or producible as a custom intermediate.
- Guide URL: https://www.malongchemicals.com/guides/cas-search-guide-chemical-procurement/

CAS 17715-69-4 is the registry number for 1-bromo-2,4-dimethoxybenzene, a halogenated aromatic building block with methoxy-substituted aryl chemistry.

We supply 1-bromo-2,4-dimethoxybenzene (CAS 17715-69-4) as a high-purity halogenated aromatic building block. The catalogue specification is 98% min purity; formula and molecular weight are C8H9BrO2 and 217.06.

#### Quality and sourcing notes
- Confirm the CAS number and synonym spelling
- Check purity, appearance and residual solvent specification
- Confirm packaging, MOQ and shipping terms
- Request COA and MSDS with the quotation
#### Frequently asked questions
